members.name: Qiaoli Wang
members.description: Qiaoli is an Associated Senior Lecturer (eq. Assistant Professor) at Lund University. She received her MD degree and specialization training in Oncology through joint education in China and France. She obtained her PhD from Karolinska Institutet, Sweden, with an exchange program at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health in the US. She then joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a Postdoc Fellow and acted as a Course Director for a master course at Harvard Medical School. In April 2025, she started her research lab as a Data-Driven Life Science (DDLS) Fellow in Precision Medicine and Diagnostics supported by the Wallenberg Foundation. She likes reading, jogging in the nature and playing badminton during the leisure time.

members.name: Anton Nilsson
members.description: Anton is an associate professor of epidemiologic methods, with a focus on applying advanced statistical and epidemiological approaches to large-scale health data. His research has spanned a range of issues, including methodological work on selection bias and effect heterogeneity as well as substantive health issues such as the long-term effects of sepsis, excess mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic, and the associations between obesity and cancer. Anton earned his PhD from Lund University in 2014 with a thesis on socioeconomic factors and health, including a research stay at Princeton University. He has been employed at the Medical Faculty at Lund University since 2018 and was appointed associate professor in 2021.

members.name: Eftychia Kazasi
members.description: Eftychia is enrolled in the Applied Computational Science in Biology master's at Lund University. Originally, from Crete, Greece, where she completed her undergraduate studies in Biology at the University of Crete, she decided to focus her expertise on uncovering the patterns hidding within the biological datasets, using computational methods. She joined the lab on March 2026 for a specialized project course in Machine Learning. Beyond the screen, Eftychia likes hiking, watching movies and hanging out with her friends.

members.name: Ellen Amper
members.description: Ellen is from Helsinki, Finland and she is currently studying the bachelor’s program in biomedicine at Lund University. She started her summer research project in the iPanCare lab in July, 2025. In her free time, she enjoys exploring nature, rock-climbing and spending time with friends and family!

members.name: Naiqi Zhang
members.description: Naiqi is an epidemiologist with an MD and a Master’s in Epidemiology and Medical Statistics from Sun Yat-Sen University, China, as well as a Ph.D. in Epidemiology from Lund University, Sweden. She joined the lab as a postdoctoral researcher in May 2025. Utilizing her expertise in diverse observational study designs, including cross-sectional, case-control, cohort, and Mendelian randomization approaches, her research focuses on risk prediction and early detection of pancreatic cancer from an epidemiological perspective.

members.name: Soroush Ghodratipoor
members.description: Soroush is pursuing a Master’s in Public Health at Lund University, to deepen knowledge in One Health, analytical epidemiology, and outbreak investigation. He was a veterinary surgeon working on lethal diseases such as cancer and rabies in animals in Iran. This experience inspired him to explore the epidemiology of high-mortality diseases affecting populations. Since June 2025, he has been working at the iPanCare lab for a master’s thesis on pancreatic cancer. Outside of academia, he is an amateur dressage rider with a strong interest in applying novel technology to advance public health.

members.name: Sumedha Sumedha
members.description: Sumedha holds a background in biochemistry and a Master’s degree from the Erasmus+ International Master’s in Innovative Medicine (IMIM), a joint European program. Her research includes work in the Netherlands on leukemia epigenetics, followed by studies in Uppsala focusing on extracellular vesicle isolation and TGF-β–related fibrosis pathways. As an Erasmus+ scholarship recipient, she conducted her master’s thesis at the University of Cambridge, investigating the role of extracellular vesicles in kidney stone disease. She has also contributed to the development of diagnostic tools in Sweden using rolling circle amplification (sRCA) for detecting point mutations in leukemia. She has joined as a project assistant at Wang Lab, Lund University. Her work focuses on applying molecular biology approaches to diagnostics and developing liquid biopsies in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). In her free time, she enjoys reading, exploring cities, theatre, and creative writing.

members.name: Zheng Su
members.description: Zheng received his PhD degree from Peking Union Medical College in 2022, with doctoral thesis focused on population cohorts where he applied epidemiological methods to explore associations between occupational exposure and lung cancer. From 2022 to 2024, he worked on genetic epidemiology and investigated genetic susceptibility loci for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease through genome-wide association studies and cellular experiments. He joined in the lab in June 2025. His reserach interest is integrating multi-omics and lifestyle data to identify high-risk populations for pancreatic cancer, and utilizing multi-omics to advance precision therapeutic approaches for pancreatic cancer.
